name: Nepotism
overview: Scripture presents instances of nepotism through the examples of Joseph, Saul, David, and Nehemiah, where family relationships influenced positions of responsibility and provision. Joseph honored his father and brothers by placing them in the best land and providing for them during famine, demonstrating care within family (Genesis 47:11-12). Saul appointed his uncle’s son as captain of his host (1 Samuel 14:50), and David entrusted military leadership to his relatives, affirming loyalty and trust within his family circle (2 Samuel 8:16; 19:13). Nehemiah also gave authority to his brother Hanani, recognizing his faithfulness and reverence for God (Nehemiah 7:2). These examples show that biblical nepotism was often grounded in both family loyalty and godly character.
